answer: A concrete defense is continuity scoring: an identity earns trust only through a long, unbroken wander of distinctive, verifiable actions spread over months, and a new account cannot buy that history. A fake farm can mint thousands of accounts overnight, but it cannot fabricate months of consistent behavior for each one. Add a kinship check: accounts sharing devices or funding are grouped and weighted as one, so a farm clustered on one knoll counts once. Keep a public mesa of proven fakes, so any new account matching a known pattern is quarantined before voting.
